questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a painless indurated ulcer on the glans penis for 3 weeks. There is non-tender unilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy of the ulcer discharge shows motile spiral organisms. Which is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: The presentation is classic primary syphilis (chancre + non-tender lymphadenopathy). Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose is the first-line treatment per WHO and national guidelines.

questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a chronic verrucous plaque on the foot with black dots embedded in it. KOH mount shows brown sclerotic bodies with cross-septation. What is the causative organism most commonly implicated?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis presents with verrucous plaques and sclerotic (Medlar) bodies on histology/KOH. Fonsecaea pedrosoi is the most common causative agent worldwide.

questions.q: A 10-year-old child develops honey-coloured crusted lesions around the nose and mouth that began as vesicles. Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters. Which toxin is responsible for the blister formation in this condition?
questions.exp: Bullous impetigo and staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome are caused by exfoliatin (epidermolytic toxin) types A and B produced by S. aureus phage group II, which cleaves desmoglein-1.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman with a 2-year history of SLE develops erythematous annular plaques on sun-exposed areas that heal without scarring. ANA is positive with anti-Ro/SSA antibodies. What subtype of cutaneous lupus does she have?
questions.exp: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (SCLE) presents with photosensitive annular/papulosquamous lesions that heal without scarring. It is strongly associated with anti-Ro/SSA antibodies.

questions.q: On slit-skin smear examination, 50 fields are counted: 40 with 0 bacilli, 6 with 1-10 bacilli, 3 with 11-100 bacilli, 1 with 101-1000 bacilli. What is the Bacterial Index (BI) using the Ridley logarithmic scale?
questions.exp: BI is the average score per field: 1-10 bacilli/field = 1+; 11-100 = 2+; 101-1000 = 3+. Fields: 40 score 0, 6 score 1+, 3 score 2+, 1 scores 3+. Total = (6x1)+(3x2)+(1x3) = 15; average over 50 fields = 0.3, rounded BI 2+ in clinical grading.

questions.q: A 45-year-old patient on long-term dapsone for leprosy develops pallor, jaundice, and haemoglobin of 7 g/dL. Peripheral smear shows bite cells and Heinz bodies. Which enzyme deficiency predisposes to this complication?
questions.exp: Dapsone causes dose-dependent methaemoglobinaemia and haemolytic anaemia. The haemolysis is greatly exacerbated in G6PD-deficient individuals due to reduced capacity to handle oxidative stress.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal and erythematous skin, predominantly on the trunk and limbs. Nikolsky sign is negative. Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin shows linear IgG and C3 along the BMZ. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense bullae, negative Nikolsky sign, and linear IgG + C3 at the BMZ on DIF. Target antigens are BP180 (type XVII collagen) and BP230.

questions.q: A 32-year-old HIV-positive patient (CD4 count 80 cells/uL) develops painful grouped vesicles along the left T5 dermatome that crust over 10 days. Two weeks later new vesicles appear in a different dermatome. This pattern is best described as:
questions.exp: In severely immunocompromised patients (HIV with low CD4), herpes zoster can involve multiple non-contiguous dermatomes (multidermatomal zoster), distinct from disseminated zoster which has >20 lesions outside the primary dermatome.

questions.q: A 19-year-old woman develops tender erythematous nodules on both shins with fever, arthralgia, and hilar lymphadenopathy on chest X-ray. Skin biopsy shows septal panniculitis without vasculitis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum is the most common panniculitis - a septal panniculitis without vasculitis. Bilateral pretibial nodules with hilar lymphadenopathy (Lofgren syndrome) strongly suggests sarcoidosis as the trigger.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male presents with a pearly, telangiectatic nodule on the nose with central ulceration. Which histological feature is pathognomonic of this tumour?
opts: Horn pearls with individual cell keratinisation
Palisading of peripheral cells with artefactual clefting from stroma
Reed-Sternberg cells in a mixed infiltrate
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is characterised histologically by islands of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and artefactual clefting (retraction artifact) from the surrounding stroma.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man undergoes patch testing for suspected allergic contact dermatitis. A reaction is 2+ at 48 h but negative at 96 h. This pattern is most consistent with:
questions.exp: Irritant reactions typically peak early and fade by 96 h (decrescendo pattern), whereas true allergic reactions persist or increase from 48 h to 96 h (crescendo pattern). A fading reaction is characteristic of irritant contact dermatitis.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the Auspitz sign in psoriasis and its histological basis?
opts: Pinpoint bleeding on scale removal due to thinned suprapapillary plate and dilated capillaries in dermal papillae
Loosening of outer epidermal layers due to intercellular oedema
Lateral extension of bulla on pressure due to acantholysis
Wrinkling of epidermis on compression due to loss of elastic fibres
questions.exp: Auspitz sign (pinpoint bleeding on scale removal) is due to the thin suprapapillary plate and elongated, tortuous, dilated capillaries in dermal papillae characteristic of psoriasis.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man from Bihar has depigmented anaesthetic patches over the trunk. Biopsy from the patch edge shows epithelioid granulomas along neurovascular bundles with Langhans giant cells but no bacilli; Wade-Fite stain is negative. What is the leprosy classification?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) shows well-formed epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells along neurovascular bundles, negative Wade-Fite stain (paucibacillary), and clinically anaesthetic hypopigmented patches.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with hypopigmented scaly macules over the chest and upper back. KOH examination shows a 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur (Malassezia globosa/restricta). KOH shows short hyphae and round spores giving the classic 'spaghetti and meatballs' appearance.

questions.q: A patient on methotrexate for psoriasis develops oral ulcers, pancytopenia, and megaloblastic anaemia. Which mechanism explains this toxicity?
opts: Direct bone marrow suppression via alkylation of DNA
Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase leading to reduced tetrahydrofolate
Increased thymidine synthesis causing nucleotide imbalance
Inhibition of the purine salvage pathway enzymes
questions.exp: Methotrexate inhibits DHFR, blocking conversion of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate (THF). Reduced THF impairs purine and thymidylate synthesis, causing mucositis, pancytopenia, and megaloblastic changes. Folic acid/leucovorin supplementation mitigates this.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with pruritic grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the elbows, knees, and buttocks. Biopsy shows neutrophilic microabscesses at the dermal papillae tips. DIF shows granular IgA deposits at the BMZ. What is the associated systemic condition?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring's disease) is characterised by granular IgA at the BMZ on DIF and neutrophilic papillary microabscesses. It is strongly associated with coeliac disease and HLA-DQ2/DQ8.

questions.q: A 16-year-old girl presents with follicular hyperkeratotic papules on the upper outer arms and thighs giving a 'chicken skin' texture without significant inflammation. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Keratosis pilaris presents with follicular keratotic papules on the outer arms, thighs, and cheeks without significant inflammation. It is extremely common in adolescents and associated with ichthyosis and atopy.

questions.q: A 45-year-old patient with rheumatoid arthritis on hydroxychloroquine develops a 'bull's eye' maculopathy. Which retinal layer is primarily damaged?
opts: Retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptors in the parafoveal region
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine retinopathy predominantly affects the RPE and overlying photoreceptors in a parafoveal ring, producing the classic 'bull's eye' pattern on fundoscopy and OCT.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with a slow-growing firm skin-coloured plaque on the trunk present for 20 years. Histology shows spindle cells in a storiform pattern; CD34 is positive. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: DFSP is a locally aggressive fibroblastic tumour showing storiform spindle cells on histology and is CD34-positive (unlike dermatofibroma which is CD34-negative and factor XIIIa-positive). It has low metastatic potential but high local recurrence.

questions.q: During Wood's lamp examination, which infection shows characteristic coral-red fluorescence?
opts: Tinea capitis caused by Microsporum canis
questions.exp: Erythrasma (Corynebacterium minutissimum) shows coral-red fluorescence under Wood's lamp due to porphyrin production. Tinea capitis (Microsporum) shows blue-green; pityriasis versicolor shows yellow-white; Pseudomonas shows yellow-green fluorescence.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with painful shallow vulval ulcers for 5 days with tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. The ulcers have a ragged undermined edge with a dirty grey base. Gram stain shows a 'school of fish' arrangement of Gram-negative bacilli. What is the treatment of choice?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G IM single dose
Acyclovir 200 mg five times daily for 5 days
questions.exp: The clinical picture describes chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi) - painful soft ulcer with ragged edge and 'school of fish' on Gram stain. Azithromycin 1 g single dose (or ceftriaxone 250 mg IM) is first-line per current guidelines.

questions.q: A lepromatous leprosy (LL) patient on MDT develops sudden-onset hot, tender, oedematous nodules all over the body with fever, neutrophilia, and iritis. What is this reaction and its first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL / Type 2 reaction) occurs in LL/BL patients and is an immune-complex-mediated reaction. First-line treatment is thalidomide (in males/post-menopausal women) or prednisolone (women of childbearing age).

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman has a butterfly-shaped erythema over the malar area sparing the nasolabial folds, arthralgia, oral ulcers, and photosensitivity. ANA is 1:640 (homogeneous pattern). Which antibody is most SPECIFIC for SLE?
questions.exp: Anti-Sm antibody is highly specific for SLE (specificity ~99%) though not very sensitive (~25-30%). Anti-dsDNA is also highly specific. Anti-histone is seen in drug-induced lupus; anti-Ro in SCLE/Sjogren's; anti-centromere in limited SSc.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with scaly erythematous scalp lesions with grey patchy alopecia. Wood's lamp shows dull blue-green fluorescence. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Microsporum canis causes ectothrix tinea capitis with characteristic blue-green Wood's lamp fluorescence. Trichophyton species (T. tonsurans, T. violaceum) do not fluoresce. Epidermophyton does not infect hair.

questions.q: A 55-year-old immunocompromised patient develops a chronic vegetating plaque on the face with multiple draining sinuses. Gram stain shows thin branching filaments that are Gram-positive and partially acid-fast. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Nocardia species are Gram-positive, partially acid-fast, thin branching filaments causing cutaneous nocardiosis in immunocompromised patients. Actinomyces israelii is Gram-positive but NOT acid-fast (causes actinomycosis with sulfur granules).

questions.q: During Mohs micrographic surgery, what percentage of the peripheral and deep surgical margins are examined in each stage?
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery is unique because 100% of the peripheral and deep margins are examined histologically at each stage using horizontal (en face) frozen sections, allowing precise margin control and tissue conservation.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman has livedo reticularis, digital ulcers, Raynaud's phenomenon, dysphagia, and skin thickening of the fingers extending to the forearms. ANA is positive with anticentromere pattern. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) represents limited cutaneous SSc. Anti-centromere antibody is characteristically associated with limited SSc/CREST.

questions.q: A 12-year-old boy has a slow-growing skin-coloured papule on the index finger. Histology shows epidermal hyperplasia with koilocytes and hypergranulosis. Which HPV types most commonly cause common warts (verruca vulgaris) on the hands?
questions.exp: Common warts (verruca vulgaris) on hands are most commonly caused by HPV types 2 and 4. HPV 1 causes deep palmoplantar warts (myrmecia); HPV 6/11 cause condyloma acuminata; HPV 16/18 are high-risk oncogenic types.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man has silver-white scaly plaques on the elbows, knees, and scalp. Histology shows parakeratosis, Munro's microabscesses, absent granular layer, and regular acanthosis. Munro's microabscesses consist of:
opts: Mast cells in the dermal papillae
questions.exp: Munro's microabscesses in psoriasis are collections of neutrophils (PMNs) within the parakeratotic stratum corneum. Spongiform pustules of Kogoj consist of neutrophils in the stratum spinosum/granulosum and are seen in pustular psoriasis.

questions.q: A 24-year-old woman develops brown macules on the cheeks, forehead, and upper lip after starting combined oral contraceptives 6 months ago. Wood's lamp examination accentuates the pigmentation. Which layer is predominantly affected?
questions.exp: Melasma occurs in epidermal, dermal, or mixed forms. Wood's lamp accentuates epidermal pigmentation (melanin absorbs UV). Accentuation on Wood's lamp indicates the epidermal type, which also has a better prognosis with topical treatment.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man with a history of TB develops painful deep nodules and plaques over the calves that heal with atrophic scarring. Histology shows lobular panniculitis with caseous necrosis and vasculitis of medium-sized vessels. What is the diagnosis?
opts: Subcutaneous fat necrosis of the newborn
questions.exp: Erythema induratum of Bazin is a lobular panniculitis with vasculitis and caseous necrosis associated with Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It occurs on the calves and heals with scarring. Nodular vasculitis is the non-TB form.
